description: The beastkin are animal-folk -- another of the continent's nonhuman kindreds, alongside the humans and the dragonkin. Where the dragonkin descend from a dragon-progenitor, the beastkin take the forms and natures of beasts. The HYENADIN (hyena-kin) are one such people, and a rival hostile to the dragonkin: it is their attack on the tribe's camp, near the story's end, that draws Kaelen into breaking his century of restraint and spends his life.
rules: Largely open -- built only as far as the story needs so far. Fixed: the hyenadin are a rival tribe who assault the dragonkin camp at the climax; the dragonkin, permitted only to defend, are gravely vulnerable to such an attack (to fight back in earnest deepens the curse), which is exactly why it becomes lethal and why Kaelen's aggressive fire is both salvation and self-destruction.

details.The hyenadin: Hyena-beastkin. Rival and hostile to the dragonkin; the aggressors in the climactic camp attack. Likely dynamic (to confirm): scavenger-predators who prey on the weak, drawn to a cursed, defense-bound people who cannot strike back without damning themselves -- the curse's defense-only law turned into a hunting weakness.
details.Open / to build later: Whether other beastkin peoples appear and what they are like; the beastkin's own nature, abilities, and culture; whether they are free or bound by any curse of their own; the specific reason the hyenadin hunt the dragonkin; how the climactic attack is set up earlier in the book so it does not arrive from nowhere.
